title_en: Xuzhou Lubao Traffic Facilities Manufacturing Co., Ltd. v. Xuzhou Huajian Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. and Third Party You Anqing — dispute over housing sale contract
ruling_gist_en: A party dissatisfied with a legally effective judgment, or a people's court that discovers a legally effective judgment is indeed erroneous, may only retry the case by initiating the trial supervision procedure according to law and setting aside the original judgment; otherwise, both parties shall be bound by the legally effective judgment. The parties may not assert any contention contrary to such judgment in subsequent litigation, and the people's court may not make findings or rulings inconsistent with such judgment in subsequent judgments.

full_text_en:
Xuzhou Lubao Transportation Facilities Manufacturing Co., Ltd. v. Xuzhou Huajian Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. and Third Party You Anqing — dispute over a house sale contract

[Ruling Summary]

Where a party is dissatisfied with a legally effective judgment, or where a people's court discovers that a legally effective judgment is indeed erroneous, only by initiating the trial supervision procedure in accordance with the law to revoke the original judgment can the case be retried. Otherwise, all parties shall be bound by the legally effective judgment. A party may not assert claims contrary to that judgment in subsequent litigation, and a people's court may not make findings or determinations that conflict with that judgment in subsequent judgments.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court
(2005) Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 65

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Xuzhou Lubao Transportation Facilities Manufacturing Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 160, Jinpu West Road, Xuzhou City, Jiangsu Province.
Legal Representative: Li Cheng, Chairman of the Board of the company.
Agent ad litem: You Ansheng, employee of the company.
Agent ad litem: Zhang Aiqin, legal counsel of the company.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Xuzhou Huajian Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at Room 1301, Management Committee Office, Jinshanqiao Development Zone, Xuzhou City, Jiangsu Province.
Legal Representative: Hu Zhiguo, General Manager of the company.
Agent ad litem: Wang Boting, lawyer of Jiangsu Xuzhou Jintai Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Hu Guanping, consultant of the company.

Third Party at First Instance: You Anqing, male, Han ethnicity, born on February 23, 1969, residing at Room 301, Unit 2, Building 3, Xuzhou Railway Dormitory No. 23, Jiangsu Province.

The appellant, Xuzhou Lubao Transportation Facilities Manufacturing Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Lubao Company), and the respondent, Xuzhou Huajian Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huajian Company), and the third party, You Anqing, in a dispute over a house sale contract, the Jiangsu High People's Court rendered a civil judgment (2004) Su Min Chu Zi No. 3 on May 18, 2005. Lubao Company, dissatisfied with the judgment, filed an appeal to this Court. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel and held a hearing on September 13, 2005. Agents ad litem of Lubao Company, You Ansheng and Zhang Aiqin, and agents ad litem of Huajian Company, Wang Boting and Hu Guanping, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. You Anqing was served with the summons of this Court but did not appear in court. This case is now concluded.

The court of first instance found the following facts upon trial:

On May 8, 2000, Lubao Company and Huajian Company entered into a "Commercial Housing Purchase and Sale Contract" numbered 0024999, providing that: Huajian Company would sell to Lubao Company the comprehensive building located at No. 160, Jinpu West Road, Xuzhou City, Jiangsu Province (hereinafter referred to as the comprehensive building) at a unit price of RMB 2,000 per square meter, with a total price of RMB 14,736,900. Lubao Company would pay Huajian Company RMB 8,040,000 for the housing purchase before May 31, 2000, and Huajian Company would deliver the commercial housing with a certificate of completion acceptance to Lubao Company for use before August 31, 2000. On the signing date, Huajian Company sold floors B1 to 3 (3,222.04 square meters) and floors 4 to 8 (4,146.41 square meters) of the comprehensive building to You Ansheng, who obtained the property ownership certificate.

On October 9, 2000, for the purpose of applying for a mortgage loan, Lubao Company had You Ansheng, You Anqing, and six others sign a commercial housing sale contract with Huajian Company for floors 1 to 3 of the comprehensive building. On October 31, 2000, You Ansheng, the legal representative of Lubao Company, made a written commitment to Huajian Company: "Our company needs to sign 8 commercial housing sale contracts and issue copies of 8 prepayment receipts (without payment) to apply for a mortgage loan. Please cooperate with our company in handling this matter. All expenses and liabilities arising therefrom, as well as related responsibilities, losses, and consequences, shall be borne by our company." On January 22, 2001, You Ansheng, You Anqing, and six others obtained an individual loan of RMB 6,000,000 from China Construction Bank, Yong'an Sub-branch. All signatures of borrowers on the individual housing loan notices were signed by You Ansheng on their behalf. On November 18, 2000, You Ansheng, You Anqing, and nine others entered into a commercial housing sale contract with Huajian Company for floors 4 to 8 of the comprehensive building. Agricultural Bank of China, Quanshan Sub-branch, granted a total loan of RMB 10,756,778.68 to the 11 individuals.

On January 22, 2001, Lubao Company and Huajian Company entered into a "Supplemental Agreement (I) to Commercial Housing Sale Contract No. 0024999" (hereinafter referred to as "Supplemental Agreement (I)") providing that: Huajian Company would be responsible for providing relevant documentation and arranging for a mortgage loan for floors 1 to 3 of the comprehensive building with China Construction Bank; the remaining property after the mortgage with China Construction Bank would be subject to a mortgage loan by Lubao Company with Agricultural Bank of China or another bank, with documentation provided by Huajian Company. The parties also agreed that Huajian Company should deliver the comprehensive building for Lubao Company to take over and be in custody before March 1, 2001.

On March 21, 2001, Lubao Company and Huajian Company entered into a "Supplemental Agreement (II) to Commercial Housing Sale Contract No. 0024999" (hereinafter referred to as "Supplemental Agreement (II)") providing that: Lubao Company's mortgage loan with Agricultural Bank of China, Quanshan Sub-branch, would "first repay the RMB 2,990,000 owed to Agricultural Bank of China, Yunxi Sub-branch, and simultaneously retrieve the land use certificate used by Huajian Company as collateral for its loan"; the parties also agreed on the repayment schedule for the remaining RMB 5,000,000 of the housing purchase price owed by Lubao Company to Huajian Company after Lubao Company obtained the mortgage loan.

On April 19, 2001, You Ansheng and Si Yi (the two are husband and wife) entered into an agreement with Huajian Company providing that: because You Ansheng and Si Yi were unable to bear the purchase price for floors 4 to 8 of the comprehensive building, Huajian Company agreed that You Ansheng and Si Yi would return floors 4 to 8 of the comprehensive building, and the property ownership certificates issued would be submitted to the relevant authority for cancellation. On the same day, You Ansheng and Si Yi submitted a statement to the Property Rights Office of the Xuzhou City Real Estate Administration Bureau, Jiangsu Province, stating: "Because we are unable to bear the purchase price for the comprehensive building, after consultation between the parties, we return the house and request that the property ownership certificates issued be cancelled."

On April 18, 2001, Lubao Company and Huajian Company completed the handover procedures for the comprehensive building.

The planned floor area of the comprehensive building was 7,151.37 square meters. Based on the construction drawings and on-site measurements, the actual measured area by the surveying team of the local Real Estate Administration Bureau was 7,368.45 square meters. On August 11, 1999, Huajian Company obtained a commercial housing pre-sale permit for 2,700 square meters (floors 3 to 5) of the comprehensive building. On June 30, 2003, Huajian Company supplemented the pre-sale permit procedures for the remaining area of 4,451.37 square meters based on the planned area.

In September 2002, Huajian Company filed a lawsuit with the Xuzhou Yunlong District People's Court, Jiangsu Province, demanding that Lubao Company repay the overdue housing purchase price of RMB 3,300,000. The Xuzhou Yunlong District People's Court, by civil judgment (2002) Yun Min Chu Zi No. 1664, ordered Lubao Company to pay Huajian Company RMB 2,705,407. The Xuzhou Intermediate People's Court, Jiangsu Province, by civil judgment (2003) Xu Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 1006, upheld the first-instance judgment. You Ansheng, You Anqing, and six others, for the purchase of floors 1 to 3 of the comprehensive building, obtained a mortgage loan of RMB 6,000,000 from China Construction Bank, Yong'an Sub-branch; You Ansheng, You Anqing, and nine others, for the purchase of floors 4 to 8 of the comprehensive building, obtained a loan of RMB 10,756,778.68 from Agricultural Bank of China, Quanshan Sub-branch. Both groups of loans were notarized as creditor documents with enforceable effect. At present, both banks have applied to the court for enforcement, and Huajian Company has also applied for enforcement; the enforcement procedures are all ongoing.

The court of first instance further found: Lubao Company was established by two shareholders, You Ansheng and Chen Guoyong, with You Ansheng holding 90% of the capital contribution. Xuzhou Yundu Catering Co., Ltd. was established by You Ansheng and You Anfu, with a registered capital of RMB 500,000, in which You Ansheng held 90% and You Anfu held 10%.

Lubao Company filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance, alleging: Lubao Company and Huajian Company entered into a "Commercial Housing Purchase and Sale Contract" providing that: Lubao Company purchased the comprehensive building from Huajian Company, with a total floor area of 7,368.45 square meters and a total price of RMB 14,736,900. Lubao Company paid all the housing purchase price to Huajian Company before May 31, 2000. Huajian Company was to deliver the commercial housing with a certificate of completion acceptance to Lubao Company for use before August 31, 2000. During the performance of the contract, on January 22, 2001, the parties entered into a Supplemental Agreement (I) providing for the use of the comprehensive building to obtain a mortgage loan from China Construction Bank to pay the housing purchase price, and providing that Huajian Company should deliver the comprehensive building to Lubao Company for takeover and custody before March 1, 2001. On March 21, 2001, the parties entered into a Supplemental Agreement (II) providing for the payment method and schedule for the housing purchase price. On April 18, 2001, the parties completed the handover procedures for the comprehensive building. Lubao Company has paid RMB 10,331,493 as the housing purchase price in accordance with the contract. After taking delivery of the comprehensive building, Lubao Company spent RMB 8,000,000 on a comprehensive renovation of the building. The planned construction area of the comprehensive building was 3,756 square meters, but the Xuzhou City Real Estate Administration Bureau, Jiangsu Province, only approved a pre-sale area of 2,700 square meters. In 2001, Huajian Company further partitioned the comprehensive building and sold it to You Anqing and ten others, who obtained real estate mortgage loans, rendering Lubao Company unable to obtain the ownership of the comprehensive building. Additionally, upon investigation, it was discovered that the land use right for the comprehensive building sold by Huajian Company was state-owned allocated land, which did not meet the conditions for commercial housing sales. Accordingly, Lubao Company requested: 1. Rescission of the "Commercial Housing Purchase and Sale Contract" signed on May 8, 2000, and the Supplemental Agreement (I) and Supplemental Agreement (II) signed on January 22, 2001, and March 21, 2001; 2. Huajian Company to refund the housing purchase price of RMB 10,331,493 already paid by Lubao Company, plus interest; 3. Huajian Company to compensate Lubao Company for renovation and other losses of RMB 10,000,000; 4. Huajian Company to assume liability for a one-time compensation equal to the housing purchase price paid by Lubao Company; 5. Huajian Company to bear the litigation costs in this case. The total of the above items amounted to RMB 30,662,986.

Huajian Company argued in its defense: Huajian Company only sold the comprehensive building to Lubao Company and did not sell it to any other person; the contract has been performed, and Lubao Company has taken possession and used the comprehensive building. The so-called commercial housing sale contracts between Huajian Company and You Ansheng et al. (8 persons) for floors 1 to 3, and between Huajian Company and You Anqing et al. (11 persons) for floors 4 to 8, were entered into at Lubao Company's request for the purpose of obtaining loans. Therefore, Lubao Company's claims lack factual and legal basis, and Huajian Company requested the court to dismiss them in accordance with the law.

Third Party You Anqing stated: On October 9, 2000, You Anqing purchased from Huajian Company units No. 3 on the first floor, No. 3 on the second floor, and No. 3 on the third floor of the comprehensive building, with a total construction area of 261.11 square meters. Subsequently, he purchased from Huajian Company two additional units, No. 401 and No. 406, in the same building, with construction areas of 244.32 square meters and 112.5 square meters, respectively. The subject matter of the dispute in the case of Lubao Company v. Huajian Company regarding the commercial housing sale contract is precisely the house purchased by You Anqing. The adjudication of this case is closely related to You Anqing. He requested the court to protect his rights as a third party when adjudicating the case.

The court of first instance summarized the points of contention among the parties as: whether the contract signed by the parties was valid; whether Lubao Company had statutory grounds for rescission; whether Huajian Company should compensate Lubao Company; and whether the rights of You Anqing as a third party should be protected.

(1) Concerning the validity of the Commercial Housing Purchase and Sale Contract signed by the parties, whether Lubao Company's request for rescission should be granted, and whether Huajian Company should compensate Lubao Company for losses. Lubao Company claimed that the Commercial Housing Purchase and Sale Contract it signed with Huajian Company should be rescinded, primarily on the following grounds: 1. The land on which the comprehensive building was built was of allocated land nature and could not be used for real estate development; 2. Huajian Company only had a commercial housing pre-sale permit for 2,700 square meters but sold 7,368.45 square meters of housing; 3. After signing the contract with Lubao Company, Huajian Company sold the comprehensive building to You Anqing and others, rendering Lubao Company unable to obtain the ownership of the comprehensive building, thus frustrating the purpose of the contract. Therefore, the contract should be rescinded, and Huajian Company should refund double the purchase price and compensate Lubao Company for losses. Huajian Company argued that although the land for the comprehensive building was allocated land, due to urban construction needs, it had been approved by the land management department and the real estate management department, so the contract signed by the parties should be deemed valid. When Huajian Company sold the comprehensive building, although it only had a pre-sale permit for 2,700 square meters, the sales area exceeding the permit had been recognized by the Xuzhou City Real Estate Administration Bureau, Jiangsu Province. Moreover, Lubao Company had known about the allocated nature of the land for the comprehensive building at the time of signing the contract. In addition, the validity of the Commercial Housing Purchase and Sale Contract involved in this case had been confirmed by a legally effective judgment of the Xuzhou Intermediate People's Court, Jiangsu Province. The contract signed by the parties had been performed, and Lubao Company had occupied and used the comprehensive building since April 2001, suffering no losses. Therefore, Lubao Company's request for rescission and compensation was unreasonable and should be dismissed.

The court of first instance held: When Huajian Company sold the comprehensive building, although it only held a pre-sale permit for 2,700 square meters, before the lawsuit was filed, on June 30, 2003, it had obtained approval from the Xuzhou City Real Estate Administration Bureau, Jiangsu Province, to supplement the pre-sale permit for the remaining area. Therefore, it should be determined that Huajian Company had the pre-sale qualification for the comprehensive building. Lubao Company argued that the land for the comprehensive building was allocated land and could not be used for the development and sale of commercial housing. However, the reply opinion of the relevant real estate management department indicated that the comprehensive building was a dilapidated building renovation project, a historical issue, and the department agreed to supplement the pre-sale permit. Moreover, the Commercial Housing Purchase and Sale Contract was signed on May 8, 2000, and the relevant provisions of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Commercial Housing Sale Contracts could apply. According to the spirit of Article 2 of that Interpretation, since Huajian Company had supplemented the commercial housing pre-sale permit before the lawsuit was filed, the contract should be deemed valid. Lubao Company's claim for rescission on this ground did not comply with the law and was not supported. In addition, the purchase contracts signed by You Ansheng, You Anqing, and nine others with Huajian Company were for the purpose of Lubao Company's mortgage loan with the bank; they were sham purchase contracts. There was no genuine house sale relationship between You Ansheng, You Anqing, et al. and Huajian Company. Therefore, Lubao Company's claim for rescission on the ground that Huajian Company's signing of purchase contracts with You Ansheng and ten others had created obstacles for Lubao Company in obtaining the property ownership certificate for the comprehensive building, thereby frustrating the contract's purpose, also lacked merit and was not supported. Lubao Company's claim for compensation for losses was also dismissed.

(2) Concerning whether the rights of You Anqing should be protected. The court of first instance held: A commercial housing sale contract refers to an act in which a real estate development enterprise sells housing that is either uncompleted or completed to members of the public and transfers the ownership of the house to the buyer, who pays the consideration. Although You Anqing signed a house sale contract with Huajian Company, You Anqing did not pay the consideration for the house, and Huajian Company did not transfer the house to You Anqing. Although You Anqing formally obtained the property ownership certificate, the house had always been occupied and used by Lubao Company. The purpose of the contract signed between the parties was not to purchase the house but to obtain a bank loan. This sham purchase contract did not reflect the true intention of the parties. You Anqing's claim for protection of his rights based on this sham purchase contract was not supported. In summary, the Commercial Housing Purchase and Sale Contract signed by Lubao Company and Huajian Company was valid. Lubao Company's request for rescission and compensation lacked factual and legal basis and was not supported. You Anqing's request, based on the sham purchase contract signed with Huajian Company, that his rights be protected in the disposal of this case lacked factual and legal basis and was not supported. Pursuant to Articles 55 and 85 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 8, 60, and 130 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 1 and 2 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Commercial Housing Sale Contracts, and Article 128 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court rendered the following judgment: Dismiss the claims of Lubao Company; Dismiss the claims of Third Party You Anqing. The case acceptance fee of RMB 163,325 was borne by Lubao Company; the case acceptance fee of RMB 17,655 was borne by Third Party You Anqing.

Lubao Company and You Anqing, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, filed separate appeals with this Court.

Lubao Company appealed, arguing that the facts found and the law applied in the first-instance judgment were erroneous, and requested the court of second instance to amend the judgment according to law. Its main reasons were: (1) The facts in the first-instance judgment were unclear. 1. The first-instance judgment found that Huajian Company had, before the lawsuit was filed, been approved by the Xuzhou Real Estate Administration Bureau of Jiangsu Province to retroactively complete the pre-sale permission procedures for the remaining area of commercial housing, which was inconsistent with the facts. Huajian Company did submit a report to the Xuzhou Real Estate Administration Bureau of Jiangsu Province on June 27, 2003, applying to retroactively complete the pre-sale permit for 4,451.37 square meters of commercial housing. However, only a deputy director of the Bureau indicated in writing "agree to complete the procedures, but do not issue a commercial housing pre-sale permit." Apart from this, Huajian Company has so far failed to provide any evidence that it had retroactively completed the commercial housing pre-sale permission procedures. It was clearly improper for the court of first instance to find, based solely on this contradictory personal instruction, that Huajian Company already had the pre-sale qualification for the comprehensive building. 2. The court of first instance's understanding of the relationship between Huajian Company and You Anqing and others was factually unclear. The court of first instance found that "although You Anqing and Huajian Real Estate Company signed a housing sale contract, You Anqing did not pay the consideration for the house, and Huajian Real Estate Company did not transfer the house to You Anqing. Although You Anqing formally obtained the property ownership certificate, the house has always been occupied and used by Lubao Company. The purpose of the contract between the two parties was not to purchase the house, but to obtain bank loans. This false housing purchase contract did not reflect the true intent of the parties." This was inconsistent with the facts. Ownership of a house should be confirmed and publicized according to the property ownership certificate, and cannot be confirmed by possession and use status. After You Anqing signed and performed the housing purchase contract with Huajian Company, the real estate management department issued him a house property ownership certificate, meaning You Anqing had in fact acquired ownership of the house. Moreover, You Anqing signed a housing loan contract with a financial institution, which was notarized by the Xuzhou No. 2 Notary Public Office of Jiangsu Province. After the financial institution established a mortgage on the house, it disbursed personal loans to You Anqing and ten other individuals, and directly transferred the purchase price into Huajian Company's account. Because You Anqing and the others failed to timely perform their loan repayment obligations, the financial institution had already applied to the People's Court for compulsory execution based on the notarized creditor's document, requesting appraisal and auction of all the mortgaged houses (i.e., the houses in dispute in this case). It can be seen that the court of first instance ignored the fact that You Anqing and others had paid the consideration for the house and had lawfully obtained the house property ownership certificates. Its finding that You Anqing and others did not pay the consideration for the house, characterizing the housing purchase contracts they signed as false contracts, and thereby denying the rights of third parties, was clearly erroneous. 3. The first-instance judgment found that "the planned construction area of the comprehensive building was 7,151.37 square meters; later, based on the construction drawings and on-site measurements by the Real Estate Administration Bureau's surveying team, the measured area was 7,368.45 square meters." This was inconsistent with the facts. The Construction Project Planning Permit issued to Huajian Company by the Xuzhou Planning Bureau of Jiangsu Province on July 23, 1999, indicated a construction area of 3,756 square meters. This Construction Project Planning Permit has not been amended to date. Therefore, the court of first instance's finding that the planned construction area of the comprehensive building was 7,151.37 square meters was groundless. (2) The law applied in the first-instance judgment was erroneous. The first-instance judgment ignored Huajian Company's conduct of developing and selling commercial housing on allocated land, which harmed the national interest and the interests of the commercial housing buyers. It found the contract signed between Lubao Company and Huajian Company to be valid, and found the contract signed between You Anqing and Huajian Company to be a false contract. This was clearly a misapplication of the law. When Huajian Company sold commercial housing built on allocated land to Lubao Company and the eleven natural persons including You Anqing, it should have, according to law, completed the transfer procedures or reported to the government with approval authority for approval. However, to date, Huajian Company has been unable to prove that it has completed the relevant procedures. On the contrary, Lubao Company has evidence proving that the land is still allocated land, and the houses in dispute in this case are houses that cannot be sold. Therefore, the court of first instance's findings that the contract signed by the parties was valid and that Huajian Company had the pre-sale qualification were clearly erroneous applications of the law. Accordingly, Lubao Company requested: 1. A judgment that the Commercial Housing Purchase and Sale Contract signed by the parties was invalid; 2. Huajian Company to return to Lubao Company the house purchase price of RMB 10,750,000 and interest thereon, and to compensate for decoration costs and losses of RMB 12,890,000; 3. Huajian Company to bear the case acceptance fee.

You Anqing's grounds of appeal and requests were essentially the same as those of Lubao Company.

Huajian Company argued in defense: Regarding the portion of the sales area exceeding the area stated in the pre-sale permit, Huajian Company has already completed the lawful formalities retroactively. The first-instance finding that Huajian Company had the pre-sale qualification was not improper. The design and construction drawings (area: 7,368.45 square meters) approved by the planning authority have the force of planning permission. Therefore, the comprehensive building constructed by Huajian Company was not built in excess of the planned area. As for the property ownership certificates being issued to You Anqing and others, this was entirely at Lubao Company's request for the purpose of obtaining loans. Lubao Company actively requested Huajian Company to cooperate and promised to bear all responsibilities and consequences itself. Moreover, the contract signed by both parties has already been found valid by an effective judgment. Therefore, Lubao Company's claim that the contract is invalid should not be supported. The appeal requests of Lubao Company and You Anqing lack factual and legal basis. The first-instance judgment found the facts clearly and applied the law correctly. We request that the court of second instance dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment according to law.

The facts found by this court upon second instance review: On May 8, 2000, Article 1 of the Commercial Housing Purchase and Sale Contract signed by the parties stipulated that Huajian Company had obtained the right to use the land parcel located at No. 160, Jinpu West Road, Xuzhou City, Jiangsu Province, by means of allocation, and the purpose of the parcel was a comprehensive building. On January 22, 2001, Article 7 of the Supplementary Agreement (No. 1) signed by the parties stipulated that the procedures provided by Huajian Company were solely for Lubao Company's use in mortgage loans. During the processing, all expenses, responsibilities, and consequences were to be borne by Lubao Company.

The other facts found by this court are the same as those found by the court of first instance.

Opinion of the Court: If a party is dissatisfied with a legally effective judgment, or if a court discovers that an effective judgment is indeed erroneous, the case can only be retried after the original judgment is revoked by initiating the trial supervision procedure according to law. Otherwise, both the parties and the court shall be bound by the effective judgment. The parties may not assert claims contrary to that judgment in subsequent litigation, and the court may not make findings or handle matters that conflict with that judgment in subsequent litigation.

According to the facts ascertained, it is known that before the court of first instance accepted this case, Huajian Company had already filed a civil lawsuit in the Yunlong District People's Court of Xuzhou, Jiangsu Province, in September 2002, based on the Commercial Housing Purchase and Sale Contract signed by both parties, seeking repayment of the matured house purchase price from Lubao Company. The Yunlong District People's Court of Xuzhou, Jiangsu Province, rendered Civil Judgment (2002) Yun Min Chu Zi No. 1664, ordering Lubao Company to pay Huajian Company the house purchase price of RMB 2,705,407. The Xuzhou Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province affirmed this first-instance judgment in Civil Judgment (2003) Xu Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 1006. Both the first-instance and second-instance judgments in the above-mentioned case found that the Commercial Housing Purchase and Sale Contract signed by the parties was valid, and, based on the finding that the contract was valid, ordered the continued performance of the contract. In other words, the issue of the validity of the contract and how to handle the subsequent issues had already been resolved by the legally effective judgment rendered by the People's Court before Lubao Company filed this lawsuit. That effective judgment is binding on the parties and the court. In view of this, whether Lubao Company in this case claims the contract is rescinded or claims the contract is invalid, both are contradictory to Civil Judgment (2003) Xu Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 1006. The court of first instance erred in substantively hearing the claims of Lubao Company and You Anqing, and this should be corrected.

You Anqing, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to this court. This court entrusted the court of first instance to serve the summons for trial upon him. After receiving the summons for trial from this court, You Anqing failed to appear in court without justifiable reason. Pursuant to Articles 129 and 157 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the appeal of You Anqing is deemed withdrawn automatically. Therefore, You Anqing is listed according to his litigation status in the original trial.

In summary, pursuant to Article 140, Paragraph 1, Item (3), Article 158, Item (5) of Article 111 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 186 of the Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, it is ordered as follows:

1. Civil Judgment (2004) Su Min Chu Zi No. 3 of the Jiangsu High People's Court is revoked;
2. The lawsuit filed by Xuzhou Lubao Transportation Facilities Manufacturing Co., Ltd. is dismissed.

The case acceptance fee for the first instance is RMB 50, and the case acceptance fee for the second instance is RMB 50, totaling RMB 100. This shall be borne by Xuzhou Lubao Transportation Facilities Manufacturing Co., Ltd. and You Anqing, each paying RMB 50.

This ruling is final.

Presiding Judge: Cheng Xinwen

Acting Judge: Liu Yinchun

Acting Judge: Chen Chaolun

April 11, 2006

Clerk: Wang Dongying

[Profile of the Presiding Judge]

Cheng Xinwen, Senior Judge: Born in 1963, holds a master's degree. Served as Deputy Chief Judge of the First Civil Adjudication Tribunal of the Supreme People's Court from October 2005.
